attachments.insertion_landmark: lateral coccyx and lowest sacral segment

actions: supports the posterior pelvic floor (with levator ani)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Small triangular muscle lying on the pelvic surface of the sacrospinous ligament, which it is frequently largely fused with/replaced by fibrous tissue in adults -- a well-documented degree of variable ossification/fibrosis unlike its more consistently muscular counterpart in most other mammals.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: No ultrasound-specific technique is published for this muscle in isolation; it is grouped with levator ani as a target for pelvic floor botulinum toxin injection in chronic pelvic pain, via the same transperineal or transvaginal digitally-guided routes used for levator ani, with the more posterolateral, cephalad position of coccygeus (overlying the sacrospinous ligament) used to distinguish it on palpation.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Overlies the sacrospinous ligament on the pelvic surface, posterolateral and cephalad to levator ani.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: A cadaveric nerve-mapping study localised this muscle's intramuscular nerve-dense region (the notional injection target) by body-surface projection and depth, reporting it well posterolateral to the equivalent point for levator ani -- evidence that a distinct, mappable injection target exists, even though no clinical dosing series isolates coccygeus from levator ani.
structures_at_risk: sacral plexus branches running on the pelvic surface of the ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament region
pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels, close to the ischial spine at the muscle's origin
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Cited alongside levator ani and obturator internus as a botulinum toxin target for chronic pelvic pain in a 2025 review, though no series reports outcomes for coccygeus injection in isolation -- the clinical literature treats the posterior pelvic floor as a functional unit rather than injecting this muscle individually. Recorded here as a genuine but weak lead, not an established individual technique.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Karp BI, Stratton P (2025) Toxicon 258:108336, doi:10.1016/j.toxicon.2025.108336 -- review listing coccygeus among pelvic floor muscles injected for chronic pelvic pain (PubMed); Hu X, Hu S, Wang M, Xiong W, Yang S (2022) Clin Anat 35(7):979-986, doi:10.1002/ca.23935 -- cadaveric Sihler's-staining/CT localisation of the intramuscular nerve-dense region of levator ani and coccygeus, for botulinum toxin targeting (PubMed)
